title: Aamir Khan Is Getting Married on July 5. He Thought He Was Too Old for Love.
excerpt: No baraat, no Bollywood spectacle — just a registered marriage at home, a 25-year friendship that became a romance, and the woman whose grandfather left Britain for India’s freedom.
body:
The video from Mumbai airport on June 11 tells you everything you need to know before anyone says a word.

**Aamir Khan** walks through the terminal in a black T-shirt, matching trousers, a cap pulled low, his signature spectacles. **Gauri Spratt** is beside him in a navy blue co-ord. Their fingers are laced together — unhurried, unguarded, the kind of ease you cannot fake. When the paparazzi swarm, Aamir doesn't perform. He just asks them, gently, to let him take his daughter home.

Three weeks from now, on July 5, these two will get married. Aamir confirmed it himself to *Variety India*: "The news about the marriage is true. It's on July 5."

No destination wedding. No Bollywood spectacle. No three-day extravaganza. Just a registered marriage at Aamir's Mumbai residence, with both families and a small circle of close friends present. If the reports hold, **Salman Khan** and **Shah Rukh Khan** may be among the few guests who make the cut.

> "I am at peace. Gauri and I are serious about each other and we are in a very committed space. We are partners, we are together. In my heart, I'm already married to her." — Aamir Khan, Variety India

This will be Aamir's third marriage. He married **Reena Dutta** in 1986 — they share two children, **Junaid Khan** and **Ira Khan**, and separated in 2002. His second marriage, to filmmaker **Kiran Rao** in 2005, produced son **Azad Rao Khan** before an amicable split in 2021. Both relationships ended without public acrimony, a rare thing in Bollywood, and Aamir continues to co-parent with both women.

But it's what happened *after* Kiran Rao that makes this story worth telling.

Aamir has spoken openly about the emotional toll of his second divorce. On Raj Shamani's podcast, he admitted he had given up on finding love again. "Before I met Gauri, I felt like I had aged, and who will I find in this age," he said. "My therapy started, and I understood that I need to love myself first and make myself healthy."

The twist? Aamir and Gauri had already known each other for nearly 25 years. They met through his cousin, **Nuzhat Khan**, in Bengaluru. The friendship was old and quiet. It became romantic in early 2024 — the kind of slow-burn that the man who made *Dil Chahta Hai* would probably approve of.

Aamir introduced Gauri to the world during his 60th birthday celebrations in 2025. At the time, he insisted marriage was not on the cards. Clearly, the cards have been reshuffled.

**Gauri Spratt**, 47, is no Bollywood outsider playing the part. She studied Fashion and Styling at the **University of the Arts London**. She ran the **BBlunt** salon in Mumbai after years with a salon chain in Bengaluru. She has a seven-year-old son, **Quinn**, from a previous marriage. She is now associated with **Aamir Khan Productions**.

And then there's her family story, which reads like it was written for a prestige film. Her father is of Tamil-British origin, her mother of Punjabi-Irish descent. Her grandfather, **Philip Spratt**, was a British-born Communist who sailed to India in the 1920s, embedded himself in the independence movement, and chose the country over the empire. There is something almost poetic about his granddaughter now making India her home in the most personal way possible — walking hand-in-hand with one of its biggest stars through an airport terminal, toward a quiet wedding at his house.

Aamir put it simply: "Gauri and I met by mistake and we connected and we became friends, and love happened. I thought I had my mother, kids, siblings — I have so many close relationships that I don't need a partner."

He was wrong, and he knows it.

For NRIs who've watched Aamir shape their Bollywood memories across four decades — from *Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak* to *Lagaan* to *3 Idiots* — there's something quietly reassuring about this chapter. The man who taught a generation that love is worth fighting for has, at 60, decided to believe it himself. The ceremony is three weeks away. The guest list is tiny. The spectacle is nonexistent. And somehow, that's the most Aamir Khan thing about the whole story.
